title: Short Stuff: Beethoven’s DNA
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 2023 research into Beethoven's DNA, extracted from eight alleged locks of his hair. Researcher Tristan Begg (UC Santa Cruz biological anthropology student) pieced together fragmented DNA since the hair lacked roots. Two locks with strong provenance records matched each other, and three others matched genetically; one was from a woman and one was probably not Beethoven's (and had previously been used to claim lead poisoning). Findings: hearing loss was not genetic, but genetic markers linked to cirrhosis (two copies of PNPLA3 variant), hemochromatosis gene variants, and evidence of hepatitis B in his final months. Researchers concluded his drinking was likely normal for the time and his liver disease was genetic. The hosts also briefly discuss the films Immortal Beloved and Amadeus.

segments.title: Introduction to Beethoven's DNA research
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the news story about researchers sequencing Beethoven's DNA, mention his health problems including hearing loss, and introduce Tristan Begg.

segments.title: Challenges of extracting DNA from hair samples
segments.summary: Explains that DNA from dead people is hard to get, that teeth or the petrous bone are better sources, and that Beethoven's hair lacked roots and was cut, not plucked, so the DNA was fragmented. Begg pieced fragments together from eight locks.

segments.title: Provenance and identity of the hair locks
segments.summary: Of eight locks, five were genetically identical; two with strong provenance records are confirmed as Beethoven's, and three others are doubtful. One was from a woman, and one had previously been used to claim lead poisoning but probably was not Beethoven's hair.

segments.title: Genetic findings on Beethoven's health
segments.summary: Hearing loss was not genetic. Genetic findings include variants linked to cirrhosis, hemochromatosis gene variants, and evidence of hepatitis B in his last months. GI problems could not be tied to genetics. Jaundice attacks are noted in historical records.

segments.title: Beethoven's drinking and liver disease
segments.summary: Researchers examined historical records of Beethoven's drinking and concluded he drank a normal amount for the time, so his liver disease was attributed to genetics rather than alcohol.

segments.title: Movie chat and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts chat about the films Immortal Beloved and Amadeus, then sign off.
